subject.title: Feature: Session authentication PIN gate (framework-level tool blocking)

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in core session authentication gate that blocks tools until a trusted non-model verifier marks the session authenticated?
rationale: The request changes core auth/session semantics and config, and the security property depends on maintainer-approved secret handling, verifier design, transcript redaction, and reset behavior rather than a mechanical hook addition.

options.title: Sponsor a core session-auth design
options.body: Add an opt-in core gate with an approved secret source, trusted native command or internal verifier, `SessionEntry` auth state, `/new` and `/reset` reset behavior, docs, and focused security/session tests.

options.title: Keep it as a plugin pattern for now
options.body: Document how `before_tool_call`, approval, and session hooks can implement deployment-specific PIN gates without adding a new core config surface.

options.title: Fold it into broader guardrails work
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/72741 or a successor design as the canonical owner if maintainers want a general external security-check interface instead of a PIN-specific feature.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a core session-auth design
recommendation.body: Add an opt-in core gate with an approved secret source, trusted native command or internal verifier, `SessionEntry` auth state, `/new` and `/reset` reset behavior, docs, and focused security/session tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans security boundary, product shape, and session/core ownership, and history shows this person on both before-tool-call and session-state surfaces.
